claim: P5 algorithm-vs-stack ratio ROBUSTNESS audit on iter-193 headline (60.6x reward, 10.3x zvf, 4.8x len). 4 paired-bootstrap stress tests (B=2000, seed 20260706, 95% CI) on 15 (ch x stack axis) cells: paired-bootstrap CI on the ratio excludes 1.0 on zvf AND reward for at least one axis (H1 PASS); excludes 3.0 (H2 PASS); the DOMINANT axes (model_family / task_slice / G) each individually carry the signal (H3 PASS); NOISY axes (seed / temperature) DO NOT exclude 1.0 on any channel because their eta^2 is approx 0 (H4 PASS scope-clarification). Drop a dominant axis -> OTHER dominant axes still exclude 1.0 (H5' PASS): drop task_slice -> G still excludes 1; drop model_family -> task_slice still excludes 1 on reward; drop G -> task_slice still excludes 1 on zvf. Signal propagates, not a single-axis artifact. Naive jackknife over ALL axes (H5 FAIL): once you remove the dominant axis, the worst remaining is seed/temperature and comparison degenerates. Naive 5-axis composite (additive main-effects, Cohen 1973 / Hays 1973) gives eta^2_composite = 0.0441 (zvf), 0.0316 (reward); ratio CI includes 1.0 for both (H6 FAIL): averaging noisy axes dilutes signal below detection. Even 3-dominant-axis composite gives eta^2 = 0.1211 (zvf, 2.67x), 0.0877 (reward, 11.75x); zvf still fails because dominant axes are correlated. Sharp reading: iter-193 headline is NOT a single-axis cherry-pick (H5' PASS) but is axis-conditional (H5/H6 FAIL): holds for axes actually varied (task_slice / model_family / G) and degenerates for axes not varied (seed / temperature). 'Report the Stack' is correct CONDITIONAL on which stack axes are varied -- the label-vs-stack ratio is a property of the experimental design, not a universal constant.

claim: P8 base-rate stress test on V-stat feature lift: lift is robust to base-rate shift (0.5% to 5.0%). 5 fsets x 6 rates x 3 seeds x 5 resamples = 450 cells; c=100. 4 hypotheses: H1 PASS (gap at 0.5% = -$0.0079/tx CI negative), H2 PASS (gap at 5.0% = -$0.0190/tx CI negative), H3 FAIL (V_max retention at 5.0% is 78% > 75% threshold — V_max loses dominance at high base rates), H4 PASS (gap magnitude grows 2.4x with rate, monotonic 0.5%→5.0%). Sharp F1+F2: V-stat lift is robust and INCREASES with base rate (20raw min-cost rises 49% across rates; 24full stays flat at 11% variation — V-stat features neutralize the FN problem at high base rates). Sharp F3: V_max dominance is RATE-CONDITIONAL — at low rates (≤2.0%) V_max captures 57-67% of lift (consistent with iter-196 57%); at high rates (≥3.0%) V_max retention climbs to 74-78%, other V-stat features become relatively more important. Sharp F4: 4sensor (no raw) is uniformly WORSE than 20raw at every rate (gap +$0.123 to +$0.210/tx), confirming iter-188's finding that V-stat features ENHANCE the raw block, don't replace it. Operational: deploy V_max alone for low-risk deployments (base rate ≤2.0%); deploy full 4-sensor stack for high-risk deployments (base rate ≥3.0%); never deploy 4sensor without raw.

claim: SYNTH D22 cross-pillar decision rule under cost-optimal operational weighting: weight each N2 (method, step) cell by w(m, s) = reward / (1 + (c/100) * mean_len / ref_len) (c=100 from P8 iter-188 framework). 5 hypotheses: H1 PASS (P5↔P8 ρ tightens 0.919 → 0.980 under weighting), H2 FAIL (raw=weighted two-cluster score=2, weights sharpen but don't introduce new alignment), H3 PASS (per-decile ρ variance 0.341 → 0.179, -47% reduction), H4 FAIL (cost-weighting INVERTS D21 decile structure: low |ρ|=0.633 < high |ρ|=0.700 vs raw low=0.622 > high=0.556), H5 FAIL (best method slightly less stable: 23→24 decile-to-decile changes). Sharp F1: EVERY cross-pillar ρ tightens — P5↔P6 -0.629→-0.879, P5↔P7 +0.951→+0.991, P5↔P8 +0.919→+0.980, P6↔P7 -0.618→-0.880, P6↔P8 -0.636→-0.880, P7↔P8 +0.791→+0.953. Two-cluster structure preserved AND strengthened. Sharp F2: D21's wide CIs were partly an artifact of unweighted averaging — under cost-weighting CIs narrow (variance drops 47%). Sharp F3 INVERSION: cost-weighting pushes weight toward high-reward cells making them the regime where methods diverge — operationally, the cross-pillar decision rule is more reliable in LOW-reward cells under cost-weighting, the deployment regime where you'd actually want to trust the rule. Cross-paper coupling: validates D20 at operational granularity; reconciles D21's wide CIs as averaging artifact; propagates P8 iter-188 c=100 cost-asymmetric framework to cross-pillar decision rules.

claim: P5 task-slice stratified algorithm-vs-stack variance ratio: stratify iter-193's headline (60.6x reward, 10.3x zvf, 4.8x len) by task_slice (gsm8k_easy / gsm8k_hard / humaneval_subset) on the 98 mega cells + N2 4-method panel. 5 hypotheses: H1 FAIL (point ratio NOT >1 on every cell — humaneval zvf/reward structurally zero because all 34 cells have mean_reward=0.0 and zvf=1.0); H2 PASS (CI excludes 1 on >=2/3 tasks per channel); H3 PASS (between-task variance huge: zvf=101.7, reward=5885.2, len=381.8); H4 PASS (top axis consistent >=2/3 per channel — model_family dominates reward everywhere defined); H5 PASS (zvf top axis varies: G dominates gsm8k slices, degenerate on humaneval). 4/5 PASS + 1 sharp FAIL — the H1 FAIL IS the headline paper-grade finding: iter-193's corpus-wide 60.6x ratio is the GSM8K slice average; on humaneval (coding task where every model scores 0) the ratio is structurally zero (no variance → eta^2=0). Per-(task, channel) ratios: gsm8k_easy zvf=19.5x [6.0, 85.2] / reward=133.0x [12.6, 548.5] / len=51.1x [3.4, 228.5]; gsm8k_hard zvf=14.1x [4.5, 66.8] / reward=132.8x [12.8, 573.7] / len=34.3x [2.2, 152.6]; humaneval zvf=0.0x / reward=0.0x / len=73.2x [6.7, 312.5]. Sharp F1 (HEADLINE): iter-193's corpus-wide ratio is task-conditional — MIN-REPORT's 'Report the Stack' thesis is trivially true on degenerate tasks. Sharp F2: completion-length is the only task-robust channel (34-73x on every slice, all CIs exclude 0 substantially). Sharp F3: G dominates zvf within GSM8K (eta^2=0.887 gsm8k_easy, 0.641 gsm8k_hard); the iter-193 finding holds within GSM8K but NOT corpus-wide. Sharp F4: model_family dominates reward everywhere defined (eta^2>=0.99 on both GSM8K slices); strongest single-task pattern in the corpus. Operational: report per-task ratios not corpus-wide averages; deploy len-based MIN-REPORT validation as task-robust fallback when reward is degenerate. Cross-paper coupling: qualifies iter-193 corpus-wide headline; closes iter-197 task-stratification recommendation; reinforces iter-189 manifest sufficiency (task_slice is the task-conditional carrier); iter-5 mega-eta^2 corpus heterogeneity; FRONTIER Round 1 critic-degeneracy hypothesis (zero-reward regime IS the critic-degeneracy regime — eta^2_stack=eta^2_algo=0 at zero reward).
